questions.question: How does Isaiah 61 begin (later read by Jesus in Nazareth)?
options: 'Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God; speak tenderly to Jerusalem and cry aloud to her of her warfare'
'Woe to the raging nations that storm, and to the many peoples who plot in vain against the LORD and his ways'
'The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor'
'Arise and shine, for your great light has now come, and the glory of the LORD has risen and dawned upon you'
questions.answer: 'The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor'

questions.question: What does the anointed one proclaim in Isaiah 61?
options: Sure judgment upon all the nations and the great day of wrath
Great riches to the faithful and high honor to all the wise
Liberty to the captives and the year of the LORD's favor
A brand new temple and a fully restored and holy priesthood
questions.answer: Liberty to the captives and the year of the LORD's favor

questions.question: Isaiah 61 promises a garment of praise instead of a faint spirit and beauty instead of ashes.
The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has _____ me to bring good news to the poor.
To grant to those who mourn in Zion, to give them a beautiful headdress instead of _____.
